newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-FOCUS-RTZ-CRA to sell zinc mine.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-FOCUS-RTZ-CRA to sell zinc mine.

text.p: Global mining titan RTZ-CRA announced on Thursday it was selling its vast Century zinc deposit, beset by land claims from Australian Aborigines, for A$345 million to local miner Pasminco Ltd.

RTZ-CRA denied it was walking away from the A$1 billion-plus project out of frustration at Alia's rapidly evolving concept of indigenous land title, preferring to describe the deal as a straight commercial transaction.

"It's a commercial deal and in no way does it reflect frustration or throw our hands in the air over the native title issue," CRA Ltd managing director Leigh Clifford told a news briefing in Melbourne.

"A$345 million for the two assets is a very good return for us...and is better than what we thought was achievable," Clifford said, adding that a smaller zinc deposit nearby was also included in the sale.

CRA, part of a dual-listed entity with London-based mining giant RTZ Plc, discovered the magnitude of the Century deposit in far north Queensland state in 1990 and planned to develop a mine producing 780,000 tonnes of mainly zinc concentrate a year.
It contracted Pasminco, the world's biggest lead and zinc producer, to take about half of the mine's output from mid-1998.

Pasminco, which badly needs Century's low-iron zinc supplies to comply with a planned environmental crackdown on its big Budel zinc smelter in the Netherlands, approached RTZ-CRA about purchasing the deposit last year, the parties said on Thursday.

RTZ-CRA was at the time in the eye of a political storm over indigenous land claims and protests from miners and some conservative state governments that claims for so-called native title were bogging down resource developments.

CRA's Clifford confirmed on Thursday the deal to sell Century Zinc Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary created to develop the mine, could fall through if protracted talks between Century Zinc management and local Aborigines collapsed.
"Negotiations are proceeding and I would not want to preempt those discussions, but I think they are proceeding satisfactorily," Clifford said.
Pasminco managing director David Stewart said that under the nation's Native Title Act, attacked by critics as a brake on development, a settlement must be reached by September.
Investors took a cautious approach to the announcement, which barely made an impact on the companies' share prices.
